audit.why: 54.19% over 203 games — the largest sample in this slice. Aurora holds level 1 and level 6; Darius owns 3-5 and both item stages once Apprehend can start the Hemorrhage chain. The recorded sides match, and the packet levelChart agrees at levels 1-3 and 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named her ultimate "Between the Worlds" and never mentioned the one property of Noxian Guillotine that governs the whole level-6 fight.
audit.why: Noxian Guillotine is 120/100/80 and 'if it is a killing blow, its cooldown is refreshed for a brief duration' — so against a low team it is effectively free. It also scales with Hemorrhage stacks, meaning the same ultimate is worth far more after he has landed five bleeds on you than before.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones his all-in. Noxian Guillotine is 460 range true damage that refreshes on a kill — never fight it with bleed stacked.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three content fields (spikes[1].text, wants.you[2], mid) and whys[4] tell the player that Between Worlds makes them untargetable and lets them walk through walls, and that this is why Noxian Guillotine cannot connect at 6. Neither property exists. Riot's text gives Between Worlds a shockwave, a slow zone, and a teleport between the two sides of that zone — a specific two-point teleport, not wall-walking, and no untargetability at all.
audit.why: Against Darius the mechanic that actually decides the fight is Hemorrhage: 'attacks and damaging abilities cause enemies to bleed... stacking up to 5 times. Darius enrages and gains massive Attack Damage when his target reaches max stacks.' Noxian Guillotine's true damage is 'increased for each stack of Hemorrhage on the target' — so the counterplay is to break contact before the fifth stack, not to look for an escape after it. Apprehend (E) is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16, the longest non-ultimate cooldown in either kit; that 26 seconds at rank 1 against your 22s Across the Veil is the only cooldown gap in this lane that favours you. Decimate (Q) heals him off the outer blade on champions hit, which is what anti-heal answers.
audit.corrected: Hemorrhage stacks to 5 and enrages him; Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales with those stacks — break contact at three.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is correctly identified as the cooldown to track but is never given a number, so the advice is unactionable.
audit.why: 26s at rank 1 falling to 16s at rank 5 is a genuinely long window, and Across the Veil is 22s — at rank 1 you can leap out of one Apprehend and have W back before the next one. That stops being true by rank 3.
audit.corrected: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 to your 22s leap — by rank 5 it is 16s and the gap is gone.

audit.why: breakdown.late already carries anti-heal as core, which is right: Decimate heals off every blade hit on a champion. The addition is naming Decimate so the player knows what they are buying against.
